title: How To Plan For A Sub And Ensure Good Behavior
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin reduces the challenge of guaranteeing good behavior for a substitute teacher to three concrete steps: picking a trusted sub, keeping academics at full weight instead of lightening the load, and making sure nothing about the routine or schedule changes in the teacher's absence. He warns explicitly against simply requesting any available substitute, since many will ignore a teacher's plans and improvise their own approach, leading to complaints about misbehavior that are really failures of preparation. He frames the sub's success as an extension of the regular teacher's own classroom management: a class already well-managed under SCM will behave the same for a sub as for the teacher, while a class that is already struggling will make life hard for whoever is in the room. The piece ends by tying good substitute days to genuinely effective daily practice rather than any special sub-day trick.
points: Cultivate at least one reliable substitute (with backups) who will follow your written plan exactly, rather than accepting any available sub.
Never lighten academic expectations for a sub day; a lighter load signals to students that the day doesn't matter and invites misbehavior.
Keep sub-day lesson plans simple to execute while still holding students to the same heavy responsibilities as any other day.
Enlist a few student leaders ahead of time to help the substitute keep routines and expectations on track.
quotes: You must have at least one solid substitute teacher on speed dial and preferably a couple of backups you trust will follow your plan and schedule precisely.
Never lighten the load because you have a sub. This sends the message to your students that the day doesn’t matter, which causes silliness, misbehavior, and a whole day of lost learning.
You must choose a sub who understands the critical importance of following your classroom management plan, daily schedule, and routines to the letter.
If you follow the SCM approach, then having a substitute teacher is easy because they can follow your plan as clearly and unemotionally as you.
The good news is that the most sought-after subs will love coming to your classroom because they get to actually teach instead of babysit.
